record.paper_title: A realist view of the electron: recent advances and unsolved problems
record.original_question: How should the more subtle theoretical developments of quantum electrodynamics be incorporated into the intrinsic-properties framework for electrons, beyond the framework's proposed explanation of finite electron energy and renormalization?

evidence.quote:
It should be noted that it is not yet suﬃciently clear,
from the viewpoint of this new theory, how the more sub-
tle theoretical developments of QED shall be put into the
new framework.

Rather by careful revision of exper-
imental evidence and subtle speculation within the new
framework: a tedious task, it seems, but which is the
price paid for the insight gained into fundamental pro-
cesses.

artifact.self_contained_problem: Within a realist "intrinsic-properties" framework for the electron — in which the electron is modeled as a localized physical entity whose finite self-energy and the renormalization procedure of quantum electrodynamics (QED) are accounted for by intrinsic structural properties rather than by formal subtraction schemes — formulate a consistent extension of the framework that incorporates the more subtle theoretical features of QED beyond finite self-energy and mass/charge renormalization. Specifically, give a precise prescription (with definitions of the relevant intrinsic variables, dynamical equations, and matching conditions to standard QED observables) that reproduces, within the intrinsic-properties picture, the following QED phenomena: (i) the anomalous magnetic moment of the electron, (ii) the Lamb shift in hydrogenic atoms, (iii) vacuum polarization effects, (iv) higher-order radiative corrections to scattering amplitudes, and (v) the running of the fine-structure constant. The prescription must agree with the experimentally verified predictions of standard QED to leading nontrivial order in the fine-structure constant.
artifact.status_search_result: No published work appears to provide a complete embedding of the subtle QED phenomena (anomalous magnetic moment, Lamb shift, vacuum polarization, higher-order radiative corrections, running coupling) into a realist intrinsic-properties model of the electron. The question is framed as an explicitly unsolved program in the proposing work, and no subsequent literature was identified that resolves it.

status_evidence.claim: The problem of incorporating subtle QED developments into the intrinsic-properties framework is stated as open.
